text:
Let the atheist come and fix his gaze
on the swift cascades that fall
with thunder's crash, in the forest
that darkens day, filled with rustic harmony,
perfumes, and shadows;
on the titanic cave that awes him
with stone monsters, hidden lake,
and plunging river.
Faced with such grandeur, he will cry,
“Amazed, I believe in your sublime majesty, my God!”

Creation is a harp that sways
in tranquil vastness with eternal rhythm
and ringing song. No murmur, sound, or voice
in earth, sea, or wind fails to join
the immortal hymn's chorus.

The insect hidden in the grass,
the bird within its nest, thunder
in the cloud's entrails, even the flower
that blooms on graves—all send a note
in measured harmony ascending heavenward.

Never can man's blind arrogance,
though it drive him mad, attain
that august, sovereign power which bridles
the ocean and sets stars turning in the sky.

He may beat his brow in vain,
helpless in satanic, cursed pride;
like desperate Prometheus he will always
be pursued by desire—alas, as infinite as pain.

translation.title: At the Stone Monastery (Aragon)
